quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Go straight ahead in your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight ahead in your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: It is safest to ride straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad or trolley tracks. If you change your angle to cross, you may move into another lane and hit oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust it as needed.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.explanation: Look through every turn by turning only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC is determined by body weight, the amount of alcohol consumed, and how quickly it is consumed. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be operated during the day.
Be operated without a driver license.
Be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Provide you with an escape route.

questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see and be seen. It should protect you from wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and surface hazards. It should prevent other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When carrying a load, where should it be secured?
questions.explanation: Secure loads low to keep the motorcycle balanced.

questions.question: When taking a curve while riding in a group, what formation should you use?
questions.explanation: Groups should normally ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking a curve, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation is best for staying together while maintaining space between riders?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation allows a group to stay close together while giving each rider enough space to ride safely.

questions.question: A helmet will give you the most protection if it is all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: A helmet works best if it meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fits snugly, and has no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat, your steering will suddenly feel:
questions.explanation: Heavy steering is a sign your front tire is flat. Stop right away and check your tires.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, it should be:
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure. Attaching loads to a sissy bar raises your motorcycle's center of gravity and can affect balance.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, how far behind another vehicle should you ride?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: When following another vehicle, position yourself so the driver can see you in:
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane behind the car. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: What should motorcyclists do about the oily strip in the center of a traffic lane?

options.text: Find a lane with less oil and grease.

questions.explanation: Avoid the oily strip. It is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride to the left or right of it and still stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you:

options.text: Must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control the motorcycle if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move into the position where other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Stop at the sign or signal and proceed normally.
Flash your lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the position where other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move into the position where you become visible to other drivers at the earliest possible moment.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, ride:

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: The left side of the lane is safest when passing parked cars. This helps you avoid doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling into traffic. Be ready to adjust your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be used when sharing the lane with another vehicle.
Usually provides good traction unless it is raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides good traction unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip is usually safe to ride on, except when it is raining. The strip is about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it while staying in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles. These vehicles travel slower than 25 mph, such as construction equipment, farm machinery, or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger on your motorcycle, you should tell the passenger to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.

questions.explanation: Tell passengers to avoid talking or moving while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the rider.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Doesn't mean that they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doesn't mean that they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. A driver may look directly at you and still not see you.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: To keep your high beam headlight turned on.
To ensure that your motorcycle is painted a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep your high beam headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on during the day and night. Use your high beam whenever it is legal and safe to do so.
